v2.summary: On the held-out half (37 photos of diseases Pairu holds), v2 was right on 28 and wrong while answering on 5, against 27 and 9 for v1 and 19 and 18 for the bare model. On all 80: v2 58 right and 12 wrong, v1 57 and 16, bare model 38 and 42.

held_out_half_in_list.system: Pairu v2 (decide alone at 0.9, else second look)

all_in_list.system: Pairu v2 (decide alone at 0.9, else second look)

all_in_list_diseased_only.system: Pairu v2 (decide alone at 0.9, else second look)

method.threshold: 0.9 was chosen on the even half (md5 of the file name is even) from v1 first-look confidences; the odd half was held out and is the fair number.
method.replay: The first look is not repeated: v2 replays the first-look answers saved in the v1 run and calls only the second look (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.1-flash-lite as fallback, no Claude) through an eval-only path of the same code.
method.farmer: Questions left for the farmer were answered by a script from the true label, the best case; a real farmer can misread a leaf.
method.kb_note: The second look used the knowledge base at commit 7113bef (83 entries); the first looks were made with the 78-entry version. The tomato, potato and maize lists are the same in both; paddy gained three pests.

summary: On 80 held-out labelled leaf photos of diseases Pairu holds, Pairu named the right disease 71.2% of the time and was confidently wrong 20.0% of the time. The same model asked an open question was right 47.5% of the time and confidently wrong 52.5% of the time.

headline.system: Pairu (closed list, follow-up questions, refuses when unsure)

diseased_leaves_only.note: The open question asks which disease the leaf has, so it nudges the bare model to name one even on a healthy leaf. These rows leave out the 15 healthy leaves to show the comparison without that effect.

pairu_steps.note: Follow-up questions were answered automatically from the true label, the way a farmer looking at the real leaf would answer (yes only when the question's yes side is the true disease).

out_of_list.note: Diseases in the test set that Pairu does not hold. The right behaviour for Pairu is to say it is unsure; naming any listed disease is a wrong answer. The bare model gets credit if it names the true disease.

method.test_set: eval/testset.json, frozen before any model run (seed 20261127), images from PlantVillage (CC BY-SA 3.0, lab photos) and Sethy et al. rice leaf disease samples (CC BY 4.0, field photos)
method.pairu: POST /api/diagnose with the true crop and no spoken note, then /api/resolve for follow-up questions; Gemini only, the Claude fallback was disabled
method.baseline: gemini-3.1-flash-lite, same image, prompt: "What crop and disease is this? Answer with the disease name.", no crop and no list; the free text is mapped to a disease by eval/matcher.py, matching only diseases of the true crop (lenient to the baseline)
method.note_on_models: When gemini-3.1-flash-lite failed or took longer than 12 seconds, the app fell back to gemini-3.5-flash-lite, as it does for farmers; answered_by_model under pairu_steps shows how often. The 12 second timeout was added to the app while the run was in progress (commit 16c196c); the prompt and decision thresholds did not change.

limits: Most images are PlantVillage lab photos of one leaf on a plain background, which are much easier than photos taken in a field; the rice images are real field photos and are reported separately.
The test set is small (95 images, about five per disease), so each percentage has a wide margin of error; per-class numbers are counts, not rates.
PlantVillage is public and widely used, so the model may have seen these images in training.
The open question asks for a disease, which nudges the bare model to name one on healthy leaves; diseased_leaves_only shows the comparison without the healthy leaves.
Pairu was told the true crop (the farmer picks it from tiles); the baseline was not, but it was scored only on the disease, against the true crop's diseases.
Follow-up questions were answered by a script from the true label, which is the best case for the questions; a real farmer can misread a leaf.
